items.title: Authenticated help topics
items.summary: Help Center topics, categories, steps, and route guidance for app users.
items.body:
Your first day in PHIGuard: A short path for a clinic administrator who has never used PHIGuard before.
Create your first task: Use a task when someone needs to do a specific piece of work and mark it done.
Find and update a task: Search for a task, change its status, and leave a short note.
Start a HIPAA checklist: Assign a starter template so your clinic has a clear list of compliance work.
Complete a checklist item: Mark an item done only after the clinic has actually completed the work.
Understand the compliance program page: Know what policies, training, risk, and vendors are for.
Open a downloaded file or PDF: Find a downloaded report and open it even if you are not comfortable with files.
Invite a teammate: Add another person without giving them more access than they need.
Understand billing and trial status: Know what your billing page is telling you before you change anything.
Ask PHIGuard for help: What to send support when you need a person to look at the issue.

items.title: Route-level contextual help
items.summary: Route help panels, warnings, and tooltips shown inside authenticated PHIGuard.
items.body:
Dashboard: Your home base. Start with the items that need attention, then move into the matching page.
Onboarding: A step-by-step setup path for plan choice, legal acceptance, trial start, teammate invite, and first checklist.
Tasks: Tasks are the clinic follow-up list. Use them when one person needs to do work and leave a record.
New task: Create one clear piece of follow-up work for a teammate or clinic location.
Task details: This page shows the work, status, owner, comments, attachments, and audit activity for one task.
Compliance overview: A map of the clinic compliance program: checklists, incidents, policies, and program records.
Checklists: Assign starter templates and track compliance work by clinic location.
Checklist details: Guided mode walks through one safeguard at a time. List mode shows everything at once.
Incidents: Track privacy, security, and compliance events from initial report through resolution.
Policies: Policies are documents the clinic publishes and staff may need to acknowledge.
Compliance program: A broader program view for policies, training, risk assessments, and vendors.
Program policies: Create, publish, and review policy documents for the organization.
Training: Track workforce training assignments, due dates, and completion state.
Risk assessments: Document larger risks, scoring, owners, and follow-up work.
Vendors: Track outside companies and whether a Business Associate Agreement is needed or expiring.
Reports: Reports help you review progress and export records for internal review.
Audit log: The audit log records important actions so the clinic can review who did what and when.
Members: Invite teammates and manage what each person can access.
Locations: Locations separate work by clinic site, department, or operating unit.
Integrations: Connect Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 for supported integration features.
Billing: Billing shows trial, subscription, legal acceptance, and Stripe account status.

items.title: Reusable public pricing and trial copy
items.summary: Canonical marketing page copy for public pricing, trial, no-card, BAA, and audit posture claims.
items.body:
Per-clinic pricing. BAA at every tier.
PHIGuard gives practice administrators a calmer way to run compliance work. One clinic price, an immutable audit trail, and guardrails that generic task tools do not give you.
Every plan includes a signed Business Associate Agreement and an immutable audit trail. No enterprise contracts. No surprise scaling costs.
What should a small clinic choose first?: Most small clinics choose Essentials when they need the HIPAA baseline and not the extra structure of the higher plans.
When does Clinic make more sense?: Clinic fits better once your practice has more coordination, more users, or a need for calendar and integration support.
What pushes an organization to Group?: Group is for multi-location reporting and advanced compliance work, such as policy, training, vendor, risk, and SOC 2 evidence management.
Do you offer a custom path?: Yes. Compliance Ops is a custom path for teams that need hands-on compliance support. It is not a public price card.
Can we just start a trial instead of talking to sales?: Yes. Self-serve trial signup is the main action, and you do not need a credit card to start.

items.title: Security and trust posture
items.summary: PHIGuard keeps security claims careful. We describe the controls we have today and do not claim certifications we have not finished.
items.body:
PHIGuard keeps security claims careful. We describe the controls we have today and do not claim certifications we have not finished.

items.title: Public security posture
items.summary: Public-safe security page claims for safeguards, telemetry boundaries, audit controls, and encryption posture.
items.body:
Encryption and transport protections: App traffic runs over HTTPS, and managed infrastructure encrypts stored data at rest.
Access and identity boundaries: The product uses unique user logins and role-based access, so each action ties back to the person who did it.
Append-only audit behavior: Audit events are kept in an append-only record. They are not treated like a feed you can edit.
Marketing and app telemetry separation: Analytics stay on the public site. The signed-in product does not load third-party marketing scripts.
Access control: Role-based access and unique user logins keep clinic actions tied to a person.
Audit controls: Product activity is kept in an append-only audit record, not a feed you can edit.
Transmission security: HTTPS/TLS protects app traffic in transit.
Stored data protection: Managed infrastructure encrypts stored data at rest.
Telemetry boundary: Public-site analytics stay separate from the signed-in app.

items.title: Public subprocessor inventory
items.summary: Public inventory of providers and service-provider boundaries disclosed on the subprocessor page.
items.body:
Managed database provider: Managed PostgreSQL database hosting; Application data and audit data stored in PostgreSQL; Database provider
Sentry: Application error monitoring and alerting; Sanitized error and request metadata with PHI scrubbing enabled; Operational monitoring
Resend: Transactional email and marketing email delivery; Recipient email address and message metadata only; no PHI permitted in email content; Email delivery
Stripe: Subscription billing and payment processing; Organization billing metadata and billing contact details only; no PHI permitted; Billing provider
PostHog: Marketing-site analytics only; Public-site analytics only; not loaded in the authenticated app; Marketing analytics
